title: Quantifying Groundwater Recharge With Cosmogenic Isotopes and a Hybrid Age‐Ranked Storage Selection Model in California (USA)
content:
Abstract

Unsustainable groundwater depletion has led to the need for increased aquifer recharge operations, and improved quantification of recharge rates, particularly those that account for seasonally and annually variable recharge, reflecting changes in climate. Here, we present a hybrid age-ranked storage selection lumped parameter model (SAS-LPM) that integrates naturally occurring isotope tracers, sulfur-35 (35S), tritium (3H), and tritiogenic helium-3 (3He*), to quantify groundwater transit times and recharge rates in a valley-fill aquifer within the Livermore Valley Groundwater Basin, California. We present a time-series data set from six monitoring wells and paired these with precipitation isotope records from water years 2023 and 2024 (WY23, WY24; October 1–September 30). The SAS-LPM framework accounts for time-varying tracer inputs, capturing variability in groundwater recharge. By mapping model residuals across a wide parameter space, we identified storage selection functions and transit time distributions for each well across the study time period. The addition of 35S to 3H and 3He* tracers provided an average of 27% (41% for younger-water wells to 0% for older-water wells) reduction in uncertainty for transit time calculations. In three wells, the fraction of water recharged from WY23 (61 cm of precipitation), ranged from 0.3 to 0.9 and generally increased through summer 2024 sampling trips. In contrast, contributions recharged from WY24 (38 cm precipitation) remained low, ranging from 0 to 0.25. The difference in contributions between these water years highlights the impact of variable annual precipitation. Combining the transit times with well depth and distance from streambeds, a conservative range of recharge rates for all wells varied from 0.03 to 2.38 m/yr. The SAS-LPM framework is a useful tool for quantifying recharge rates in groundwater basins and can be an important tool for groundwater resource planning and assessment.
